copy.blurb:
The model fancies Argentina more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Algeria. +10.9pp is a wide disagreement by the engine's standards; that's what fires this as a Pick on the home side.

Public Elo rates Argentina 390 points higher than the other side (Argentina 2140, Algeria 1750). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Argentina to win at 81%, the draw at 10%, and Algeria to win at 9%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Argentina sits at 81% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Argentina to win at 70%, the draw at 20%, and Algeria to win at 10%. The Argentina side trades at 70% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of −239. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 81%, +10.9pp wider.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Argentina side that lower bound is 77% — +6.5pp clear of the market's 70%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Argentina side.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 28 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Argentina a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +10.9pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: Argentina are favourites on the market at 70% — and the model thinks the market is still underrating them. Our prior reads 81%, a +10.9pp upgrade that crosses the Pick threshold comfortably.
